name: Against Malaria Foundation (The Life You Can Save, 2025)
beneficiaries_note: The three countries of the sheet's 2024 distributions (DRC, Nigeria, South Sudan), by AMF's costs in each.

missing_data.note: Measured: AMF counts the nets it distributed in 2024 and the people sleeping under them in post-distribution monitoring, and the effect of nets on malaria deaths is from the Cochrane review of randomised trials.

summary: The Against Malaria Foundation buys insecticide-treated bednets for mass campaigns in Africa, distributed by governments and partners. The Life You Can Save estimates $93 per DALY averted in the DRC, $50 in Nigeria and $85 in South Sudan from AMF's 2024 distributions, counting under-five deaths averted at the Cochrane review's 5.6 lives per 1,000 children protected. Our view pools the three countries by money, values each death by age the site's way and discounts the net's later years; the biggest uncertainties are the deaths per case the sheet uses and how many of the nets others would have funded.

rows.label: Cost per DALY averted, South Sudan
Cost per DALY averted, the three countries pooled by money
rows.explainer: The sheet gives a figure for each country and no overall one. This is the three countries' costs over their DALYs (our pooling), so the figure is what the average dollar did: $93 in the DRC, $50 in Nigeria, $85 in South Sudan.

rows.label: Value of a death of a child under five averted, in healthy years
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The Life You Can Save counts a child's death averted as the child's remaining life expectancy at 2.5 years, discounted at 3%, about 28 years. The site values every death of a child under five the same way: GiveWell's moral weight (116.25 units of value), times the value-of-a-life slider, in healthy years at Your values' exchange rate (58 at the defaults).

rows.explainer: GBD 2023, sub-Saharan Africa (facts: death_ages).

Share of malaria deaths at five or older that are at 50 or older
Value of a malaria death at five or older averted, in healthy years
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The Life You Can Save counts a death at five or older as the remaining life expectancy at 25 (the average age of malaria deaths it cites, 25.9), discounted at 3%. The sheet lumps every age from five up, so our view weights GiveWell's moral weights by age by the ages of sub-Saharan Africa's malaria deaths over five (GBD 2023), times the value-of-a-life slider, in healthy years.

Discount rate on the years of protection
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The sheet adds up the cases and deaths over the net's years at face value; our view discounts later years at the shared rate (Your values). The Life You Can Save discounts only life expectancy, so the evaluator view keeps 0 here.

rows.label: Discounted years of protection per year counted
rows.explainer: A net's three years of protection, the later two discounted to today: at 4% the three years count as 2.89.

rows.label: Healthy years gained, deaths valued by age
rows.explainer: The sheet's deaths averted and illness averted, with each death valued by age the site's way and the net's later years discounted.

rows.label: Our healthy years for the same deaths and illness, per DALY of The Life You Can Save's
rows.explainer: The evaluator view keeps The Life You Can Save's DALYs (1).

rows.label: Share of the nets that wouldn't have reached households without AMF's money
rows.explainer: Our judgment, 85% (60% to 100%); the sheet credits AMF with every net. National campaigns are planned to reach everyone, and where AMF didn't fund the nets the Global Fund, the US President's Malaria Initiative or the government would have funded some of them, later or in part. Anchor: GiveWell's funging adjustments for AMF's campaigns, which take off between a tenth and a third depending on the country.

rows.label: AMF's share of all spending on its net campaigns
rows.explainer: Governments and partners pay the rest of a campaign's cost in kind (staff, storage, transport). With credit by share of resources on, AMF gets only its share. GiveWell's DRC figure, the range spanning its other locations.

source.title: GiveWell, AMF cost-effectiveness analysis (September 2026)

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of programme cost
rows.explainer: Default for programmes that mostly buy and hand out goods: nets are most of AMF's cost. Our judgment.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Distribution staff are hired locally at local rates. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid by AMF's donors in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources on, the governments' and partners' in-kind costs and staff's forgone pay count as part of the cost. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Healthy years gained per dollar
rows.explainer: The Life You Can Save's DALYs per dollar, with deaths valued by age and the later years discounted, times the share of the nets due to AMF and the share of the cost its donors pay.
